title: Electron shell: app menu, quit question, theme, icons, macOS hardening
owns: the application menu and nativeTheme in main.ts, windows.ts (quit question, window icons), assets/**, scripts/package/fuses.mjs and the macOS signing/entitlements

findings.title: Default Electron application menu is left on Windows and Linux: Ctrl+Q quits Ember with no 'still working' question, Ctrl+Shift+I opens DevTools in every window, Alt reveals File/Edit/View/Window
findings.area: Window chrome / keyboard shortcuts (settings, command, prompt, Ask windows)
findings.platforms: linux (verified with real key events), windows (same Electron default menu)
findings.scenario: main.ts calls Menu.setApplicationMenu only when sys.lifecycle.appMenu is true (macOS). On Windows and Linux Electron keeps its default menu: File > Quit (Ctrl+Q), Edit, View > Reload (Ctrl+R) / Force Reload / Toggle Developer Tools (Ctrl+Shift+I) / Zoom / Toggle Full Screen (F11), Window > Close (Ctrl+W). A user typing in Settings, the Ask box or a prompt who presses Ctrl+Q (or Alt+F then Q) quits Ember instantly while a task is running or SSH hosts are connected. quitEmber's 'Ember is still working on a task' question (the quit confirmation at main.ts:466) is bypassed, and will-quit stops the agent. Ctrl+Shift+I opens a DevTools window on the password and host-key prompt window and on the command window. Ctrl+W in the Ask box destroys it. Pressing Alt in Settings, the command window or the fixed 440x300 prompt window shows an Electron menu bar (autoHideMenuBar) and shrinks the content.
findings.evidence: Real Electron 44 under Xvfb: Menu.getApplicationMenu() lists File:Quit[CommandOrControl+Q], Edit, View:Reload|Force Reload|Toggle Developer Tools[Ctrl+Shift+I]|Zoom|Toggle Full Screen[F11], Window:Close[CommandOrControl+W]. XTest key events sent to the focused settings window (scratch xkey.py + ctrlq2.mjs): Ctrl+Shift+I gave isDevToolsOpened=true for the home window, and Ctrl+Q ended the process ('exited after Ctrl+Q: true'). askkeys.mjs: Ctrl+W in the focused Ask window removed it from BrowserWindow.getAllWindows(). windows.ts sets autoHideMenuBar:true on home, command and prompt.
findings.fix: On non-macOS call Menu.setApplicationMenu(null), or a minimal menu that keeps only Edit and zoom (zoom is a useful accessibility feature the default menu accidentally provides) and has no Quit, Reload, DevTools, Close or fullscreen. Do it before app ready and in the same place as the macOS menu. If a Quit shortcut is wanted, route it through quitEmber() so the question is asked.

findings.title: Windows and Linux windows keep Electron's default application menu: DevTools, reload and Ctrl+Q (which skips the quit question) are live
findings.scenario: Ctrl+Shift+I opens DevTools in the settings window, the command window or the SSH password card. The page console can then call the preload bridges, and DevTools shows what is typed in the password field. Ctrl+R reloads a command card mid-approval. Ctrl+Q quits at once through the menu's `quit` role, without the "Ember is still working on 2 tasks / running 1 command" question that `quitEmber` asks. Commands and connections then stop.
findings.evidence: Built app under xvfb: `Menu.getApplicationMenu()` lists File>Quit (CommandOrControl+Q), View>Reload (CmdOrCtrl+R), Force Reload, Toggle Developer Tools (Ctrl+Shift+I) and zoom items. Clicking the toggledevtools item gave `isDevToolsOpened() === true` on the production-built home window (probe1.mjs, probe2.mjs). `Menu.setApplicationMenu` is only called when `sys.lifecycle.appMenu` is true (macOS, line 1179). No window sets `devTools: false`. There is no `before-quit` handler, so the role goes straight to `app.quit()`. `autoHideMenuBar` hides the bar, but accelerators still work. Navigation, window.open and node access are correctly blocked: `location.href` did not navigate and `window.open` returned null.
findings.fix: Call `Menu.setApplicationMenu(null)` on win32 and linux (or give them a minimal menu whose Quit calls `quitEmber`). Set `devTools: app.isPackaged ? false : true` in every webPreferences factory (app/main/windows.ts, voice.ts, ask.ts, overlay.ts, handle.ts, desk/view.ts). Optionally add a `before-quit` handler that routes to the quit question.

findings.title: macOS build: RunAsNode stays on and the ad-hoc signature has no hardened runtime. Any process of the user can borrow Ember's Accessibility and Screen Recording grants
findings.scenario: The user grants Ember Accessibility and Screen Recording. Other malware running as the same user can run `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 /Applications/Ember.app/Contents/MacOS/Ember -e '...'`, with Ember's bundled koffi available, or inject a dylib with DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES. Electron apps are known to give such code the bundle's TCC permissions. The fuse comment says this "gives whoever starts it nothing beyond running the binary themselves", which is not true when TCC attributes the access to Ember's code identity.
findings.evidence: EMBER_FUSES keeps `RunAsNode: true` (helpers run through ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE). On Linux I ran `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 electron -e '...koffi.load("libc.so.6")...'` and got arbitrary JS with FFI in Ember's binary. mac-bundle.mjs line 103 signs with `codesign --force --deep --sign -` without `--options runtime`, so DYLD_* variables are honoured. The TCC effect itself could not be verified on Linux.
findings.fix: Sign with `--options runtime` (hardened runtime, library validation) and no allow-dyld-environment-variables entitlement. Move the AX sidecar host, job host and askpass off ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE (utilityProcess, or a separate small Node binary) so RunAsNode can be turned off. Until then, correct the comment and state the TCC caveat in the docs.

findings.title: Native window chrome follows the OS theme while every Ember window is dark-only (nativeTheme.themeSource is never set)
findings.area: Window backgrounds / native chrome per OS
findings.scenario: The settings, command and prompt windows paint #121011 (a dark surface). There is no light appearance anywhere in the CSS: no prefers-color-scheme rule, and ember.css sets color-scheme:dark. A user in Windows or macOS light mode gets a bright title bar, light native menus, and light native dialogs (the quit question, window.confirm for 'Forget host') around a near-black window. The result looks like two apps. The same applies to the handle's native right-click menu.
findings.evidence: Real Electron: nativeTheme.themeSource === 'system' and shouldUseDarkColors === false in the running app; grep for nativeTheme/themeSource in app/ finds only a gsettings read in hands/system.ts. DESIGN.md confirms the design is intentionally dark-only.
findings.fix: Set nativeTheme.themeSource = 'dark' at startup (before windows are created). That gives dark title bars on Windows 11 and macOS and dark native menus and dialogs, and it matches what the pages already assume. If a light appearance is ever wanted, that is a separate design task.

findings.title: App icon is unreadable at 16 and 24 px, and Ember's Linux windows set no icon at all
findings.platforms: windows (taskbar, Explorer lists), linux (AppImage, unpackaged), macOS (tiny Dock/menu sizes)
findings.scenario: The same SVG (a 104 px tile on a 128 px canvas) is used for the ICO (sizes 16 to 256), the iconset and the Linux PNG. The visible tile covers 81% of the canvas, so at 16 px it is a 13 px graphite square with Cinder reduced to a brown smudge and two orange dots, and the dark tile nearly disappears on a dark taskbar. On Linux the BrowserWindows are created without an icon option, so _NET_WM_ICON is empty and GNOME shows an icon only when the .desktop entry matches (RPM). Running the AppImage without desktop integration, or from a build tree, gives the generic gear in Alt-Tab and the dash.
findings.evidence: Rendered with sharp at 16/24/32/48/64/256 on white, #202020 and Windows-blue backgrounds: shots/icon-sheet.png; opaque bounding box at 256 px is 24..231 (81% of the canvas). X11 properties read from the running app (xprops.py): windows 'ember' and 'Ember' have WM_CLASS ember/ember and _NET_WM_ICON longs=0. grep for 'icon:' / nativeImage / setIcon in app/main finds none; icons only reach the exe and bundle (scripts/package/icon.mjs, stage.mjs).
findings.fix: Export dedicated 16 and 24 px (and optionally 32) artwork for the ICO and iconset: fill the canvas, no baked shadow, a simplified Cinder (eyes and the glow) and a lighter rim so it holds on dark taskbars. On Linux pass icon: path to the packaged PNG in createHomeWindow, createCommandWindow and createPromptWindow (and the other BrowserWindows) so AppImage and dev runs show it.

findings.title: macOS app menu has no "About Ember" item
findings.scenario: The Ember app menu starts at "Settings…" and has Hide and Quit, but no About item, so a Mac user cannot see the version from the menu (it is only in Settings › About this build, which only has a version line).
findings.evidence: main.ts:1180-1189 builds the template with Settings…, hide roles and Quit Ember.
findings.fix: Add {role: "about"} first, with app.setAboutPanelOptions for the name, version and licence.

findings.title: Quit question uses "it" for several tasks, and "tasks running" reads awkwardly
findings.scenario: With three tasks under way, Quit Ember asks "Ember is still working on 3 tasks." with the detail "Quitting stops it where it is." (should be "them"). The mixed branch computes the plural correctly. Elsewhere "once the tasks running are done" (home/copy.ts:67, home/main.ts:466 button "Reconnect now (stops the tasks running)", host.ts messages) is clumsy.
findings.evidence: quitQuestion(3,{commands:0,connections:0}) returns {"message":"Ember is still working on 3 tasks.","detail":"Quitting stops it where it is."}; the mixed case returns "stops them where they are".
findings.fix: Reuse the `one` logic for the tasks-only branch: tasks === 1 ? "stops it where it is" : "stops them where they are". Say "tasks that are running" in the tagline, button and host messages.
